reason: The Book of Ruth contains no passages in which Yahweh directly complains about the people. While the narrative begins with a famine (which could be interpreted as divine judgment), there is no explicit statement of Yahweh's complaint. The text does include Naomi complaining about her personal suffering (וַֽיהוָה֙ עָ֣נָה בִ֔י וְשַׁדַּ֖י הֵ֥רַֽע לִֽי - 'Yahweh has testified against me, and the Almighty has dealt harshly with me'), but this is her complaint, not Yahweh's. Additionally, there is explicit mention of Yahweh's providence and mercy toward the people (פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ עַמּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לָֽחֶם - 'Yahweh has visited his people to give them bread'). The narrative overall emphasizes divine providence and redemption rather than divine complaint.
